Copilot Practice Lab

Five exercises that build real skills. Complete at least three in your first two weeks.

AI fluency comes from practice, not theory. Each exercise below takes 15-30 minutes and produces something you can actually use. Start with Exercise 1 and work your way through.

Beginner ⏱️ 15 min

Exercise 1: The Competitive Battlecard

Create a one-page competitive comparison for a product and competitor you know well.

The Task

Pick a real competitor you face regularly. Use Copilot to create a battlecard with: positioning comparison, key differentiators, objection handles, and win themes.

Starting Prompt
I need to create a competitive battlecard comparing [your product] to [competitor product]. Context: - Our target buyer is [persona] - Key use cases are [list 2-3] - Our main differentiators are [list 2-3] Create a battlecard with these sections: 1. Positioning comparison (one paragraph each) 2. Feature comparison table (5-7 key capabilities) 3. Where we win / Where they win 4. Top 3 objections and how to handle them 5. Proof points to cite
Refinement Suggestions
  • "Add specific metrics or customer quotes we can reference"
  • "Make the objection handles more conversational"
  • "What questions should a rep ask to uncover weaknesses?"
✓ Success Criteria
  • Battlecard covers all 5 sections
  • Content is specific to your actual product (not generic)
  • You refined the output at least twice
  • You'd share this with a sales rep (maybe with edits)
Beginner ⏱️ 20 min

Exercise 2: The Executive Summary

Transform a long document into a crisp executive brief.

The Task

Find a document you've written or received recently (a report, proposal, or analysis). Use Copilot to create an executive summary that a VP could read in 2 minutes.

Starting Prompt
Summarize the following document for an executive audience. Create: 1. One-sentence bottom line (what's the key takeaway?) 2. Three bullet points with the most important findings 3. One clear recommendation or next step 4. Any risks or caveats they should know Keep the entire summary under 200 words. Use plain language, no jargon. [Paste your document here]
Refinement Suggestions
  • "Make the bottom line more action-oriented"
  • "What questions will the exec likely ask?"
  • "Reframe this for [specific stakeholder]"
✓ Success Criteria
  • Summary is under 200 words
  • Bottom line is clear and actionable
  • An exec could understand it without the full doc
  • You refined based on what was missing
Intermediate ⏱️ 25 min

Exercise 3: The Messaging Framework

Build a complete messaging hierarchy for a product or feature launch.

The Task

Create messaging for an upcoming launch or a product you're working on. Build the full hierarchy: positioning statement, value props, proof points, and persona-specific variants.

Starting Prompt
I'm creating messaging for [product/feature]. Help me build a messaging framework. Context: - Product: [name and brief description] - Primary persona: [title and key characteristics] - Secondary persona: [if applicable] - Key problem we solve: [one sentence] - Main competitor alternative: [what they'd use otherwise] Create: 1. Positioning statement (for-who-what-unlike-because format) 2. Three value propositions with supporting proof points 3. Elevator pitch (30 seconds, conversational) 4. Headlines for each persona (5 words max) 5. Three "so what" test responses (why should they care?)
Refinement Suggestions
  • "The value props are too feature-focused. Reframe around outcomes."
  • "Create a version for technical buyers vs. business buyers"
  • "What would a skeptic say? Add preemptive responses."
✓ Success Criteria
  • All 5 framework elements are complete
  • Messaging is differentiated (not generic)
  • Passes the "so what" test
  • You could present this to your team
Intermediate ⏱️ 20 min

Exercise 4: The Content Repurposer

Turn one piece of content into five different formats.

The Task

Take an existing blog post, case study, or whitepaper. Use Copilot to repurpose it into multiple formats for different channels.

Starting Prompt
I have a [blog post/case study/whitepaper] that I want to repurpose. Here's the content: [Paste content] Create these 5 versions: 1. LinkedIn post (under 200 words, conversational, includes hook) 2. Email teaser (3 sentences + CTA) 3. Twitter/X thread (5 tweets, each standalone but connected) 4. Internal Slack announcement (casual, team-focused) 5. Executive talking points (3 bullets for verbal delivery) Maintain the core message but adapt tone and format for each channel.
Refinement Suggestions
  • "The LinkedIn post needs a stronger hook in the first line"
  • "Make the Twitter thread more provocative"
  • "Add a question at the end of the LinkedIn post to drive engagement"
✓ Success Criteria
  • All 5 formats are distinct (not just length variations)
  • Core message is consistent across all
  • Each format fits its platform norms
  • At least one is ready to post with minimal edits
Advanced ⏱️ 30 min

Exercise 5: The Strategy Stress Test

Use Copilot as a critical thinking partner to pressure-test a strategy or plan.

The Task

Take a strategy, plan, or proposal you're working on. Use Copilot to find weaknesses, anticipate objections, and strengthen your argument.

Starting Prompt
I'm presenting a strategy/proposal and need to stress-test it. Here's the plan: [Paste your strategy or proposal] Act as a skeptical executive and: 1. Identify the 3 biggest weaknesses or risks 2. List questions a CFO would ask 3. List questions a skeptical peer would ask 4. Suggest what's missing from this plan 5. Rate the strength of the argument (1-10) and explain why Be direct. I need honest critique, not validation.
Follow-Up Prompts
"Now help me address weakness #1. What evidence or framing would strengthen this?" "Write a preemptive response to the CFO's first question" "What's the strongest counter-argument to this entire approach?"
✓ Success Criteria
  • You received critique you hadn't considered
  • You used the feedback to improve the plan
  • You feel more prepared for tough questions
  • The final version is meaningfully stronger
💡 Lab Tip: Save your best prompts and outputs. Over time, you'll build a personal library of patterns that work for your specific work. The prompt library page has more examples to draw from.

Submitting Your Work

After completing an exercise:

  1. Save your final output (Word doc, PDF, or screenshot)
  2. Post to the team channel with the exercise number
  3. Include one sentence on what you learned or would do differently

Goal: Complete at least 3 exercises by the end of Week 2.
